children: U.S. long bond futures have recovered from their recent low—the lowest level since 2002—according to Seeking Alpha analyst Andrew Hecht, though he noted that "time will tell whether the current recovery is a dead-cat bounce or the start of a recovery."
The Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF
rose 0.21% on Tuesday after having declined 0.81% from a month ago.
Hecht identified crude oil prices as "a critical factor for inflation," keeping the Middle East and Ukraine "in the spotlight" as key geopolitical drivers.
Treasury yields were mixed on Tuesday, with the 10-year yield
declining 2 basis points to 5.12% while the 30-year yield
dropped 5 basis points to 5.42%, according to Seeking Alpha. Crude oil futures

Looking ahead, Hecht pointed to the U.S. midterm elections as "the next significant event," noting that "polls reflect a shift in majorities in the House and Senate, which could affect the administration's initiatives, but polls have been wrong in the past."
He also warned that violent demonstrations in France "remind us that sudden surprises could roil markets across all asset classes."
The Seeking Alpha analyst advised investors to "carefully monitor the risk-reward profile on all trading and investment positions, as many factors could cause sudden volatility."
Hecht observed that bonds currently offer attractive yields, commodity prices have been rising for years, and stocks remain near highs.

title: Time will tell if current bond recovery is a dead-cat bounce or start of recovery – SA analyst
